critiques.claim: Requirements are divided into functional requirements, quality-of-service constraints, and technology constraints.
critiques.critique: The functional/nonfunctional binary is too rigid to serve as a primary taxonomy. Security, accessibility, safety, and privacy contain both required behavior and required qualities. Terminology also conflicts with BABOK (Business vs Stakeholder vs Solution vs Transition requirements).
critiques.nuance: Useful teaching heuristic for beginners to separate core domain business logic from technical implementation choices.

extensions.title: Topic 9.1 Layered Requirements Taxonomy
extensions.summary: Full 10-layer taxonomy replacing the binary functional/nonfunctional distinction.

fieldContext.note: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 replaces the 2011 edition, defining a 9-characteristic product quality model.

personalNotes: BABOK hierarchy clarifies that project constraints (cost, schedule, staffing) should not be conflated with organizational business goals.
